plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the architecture of a deep residual network (ResNet) at two levels of detail. The main diagram traces the flow of feature tensors through successive stages of the network, with labeled spatial and channel dimensions at each stage: a 7x7 convolution produces 112x112x64 feature maps, which are then processed through four residual stages yielding progressively smaller but deeper tensors — 56x56x256, 28x28x512, 14x14x1024, and 7x7x2048 — before a final average pooling and fully connected (AvgPool + FC) layer. Between stages, Subsample blocks reduce spatial resolution while increasing channel depth; within each stage, repeated ResBlocks (indicated by ellipses and annotations such as '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total') apply the same transformation many times. An inset zooms into the internal structure of a single ResBlock, showing the sequence: Conv 1x1 (bottleneck squeeze), Batch Normalization (BN), ReLU, Conv 3x3 (spatial convolution), BN, ReLU, and Conv 1x1 (channel expansion), with a skip connection bypassing these layers and adding the input directly to the output. The figure introduces the residual (skip-connection) design that allows very deep networks to be trained effectively by ensuring gradients can flow directly from later to earlier layers.

elements: input image slab 224x224x3 (tall thin plate at far left)
Conv 7x7 stride 2 + MaxPool operation label with arrow
tall brown/tan slab for 112x112x64 feature maps
Subsample arrow/label to stage 1
stage-1 ResBlock stack: several short blue-grey slabs representing 56x56x256(64) with '24 blocks total' annotation and ellipses
stage-2 ResBlock slabs 28x28x512(128) with '36 blocks total' annotation
stage-3 ResBlock slabs 14x14x1024(256)
stage-4 ResBlock slabs 7x7x2048(512)
AvgPool + FC + Softmax arrow/label at far right
final classifier bars: two thin teal vertical bars labeled 1000
dashed diagonal size labels above each slab group (224x224x3, 112x112x64, 56x56x256(64), 28x28x512(128), 14x14x1024(256), 7x7x2048(512))
zoomed ResBlock inset: rounded grey panel containing the block diagram
inset small blue input cube with '≡' expansion arrow
inset layer chips in sequence: BN (orange), ReLU (teal), Conv 1x1 (grey), BN, ReLU, Conv 3x3, BN, ReLU, Conv 1x1
inset skip-connection line bypassing the chip sequence from input to output
inset plus-sign circle (⊕) at the addition point, then output arrow

interactions.label: Residual forward pass
interactions.teaches: A pulse of signal travels down the main path through BN-ReLU-Conv bottleneck layers while a copy travels in parallel along the identity skip connection; the two recombine at the ⊕ addition, showing that the block only needs to learn the residual F(x) added to x

interactions.label: Network depth
interactions.teaches: Switching between 24 and 36 blocks grows the number of stacked ResBlock slabs in the stages and updates the 'blocks total' labels, while the tensor dimensions at each stage stay fixed — depth adds repetitions, not new shapes

Clicking a stage slab zooms into that stage's bottleneck ResBlock detail, revealing the Conv 1x1 squeeze (e.g. 64 channels), Conv 3x3 spatial processing, and Conv 1x1 expansion (e.g. 256 channels) with that stage's specific channel numbers labeled
Rotating the slab stack makes the depth-vs-resolution tradeoff legible: slabs get thinner and deeper along the channel axis while their spatial footprint shrinks from 112x112 to 7x7

demo_steps.title: Shallow network, 24 blocks
demo_steps.narration: At 24 blocks total, each stage shows its base number of ResBlock repetitions; note the fixed dimensions 56x56x256 down to 7x7x2048.

demo_steps.title: Deep network, 36 blocks
demo_steps.narration: Sliding to 36 blocks adds more slabs to the stages and updates the total label — the network gets deeper purely by repeating blocks, tensor shapes unchanged.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Oblique slab row spanning about x=-9 to x=+9, each slab a thin box drawn with the front face true (undistorted rectangle, X screen-right, Y screen-up) and depth receding up-right along +Z. Slab sizes encode dimensions: input image plate ~2.8 tall x 2.8 wide x 0.15 deep at x=-8.5; 112x112x64 brown slab (#a0522d/#b5651d) ~2.4x2.4x0.35 at x=-6.5; stage-1 stack of 3-4 blue-grey slabs (#7f9db9 faces, darker #5a7a99 edges) each ~1.6x1.6x0.25 around x=-4.5 with '24 blocks total' text and ellipses to its right; stage-2 slabs ~1.2x1.2x0.4 at x=-2.5 labeled '36 blocks total'; stage-3 ~0.9x0.9x0.55 at x=-0.5; stage-4 ~0.6x0.6x0.8 at x=+1.5, then progressively longer thin slabs to x=+5 (the source shows late-stage slabs as long low bars). Final two thin teal bars ~1.8 tall x 0.18 wide at x=+6.5 and x=+7.5, each labeled '1000'. Dimension labels sit above each group, rotated ~30deg diagonally, dark grey italic. Inset panel floats top-center: rounded-rect grey (#e8e8e8) ~7x1.4x0.1 at y=+3.2, containing input cube (~0.5 side, blue #7f9db9) at left, then 9 chips in a row: BN #d97b4f orange, ReLU #7fc4b5 teal, Conv grey #cfcfcf, BN, ReLU, Conv 3x3 grey, BN, ReLU, Conv 1x1 grey, each ~0.55x0.4x0.15; skip line arcs above chips from cube to a ⊕ circle (cross-in-circle) at right, then arrow out. Channel counts per stage: stage1 bottleneck 64, out 256; stage2 128/512; stage3 256/1024; stage4 512/2048.
interactionPlan.notes: Build slab stacks as instanced boxes whose count per stage changes with the depth slider (24: e.g. 3/4/6/3 style proportions; 36: scale up mid-stage counts), keeping slab footprint fixed. Forward-pass animation: moving glowing sphere/segment along inset chip sequence plus a second pulse along the skip arc, converging at ⊕ with a flash, then exiting — run inside the inset panel. Stage click: raycast slabs, tween camera to the stage and swap the inset labels to that stage's bottleneck/out channel numbers. Keep all text as sprites so labels stay legible during orbit.

discrepancies: Input image plate is a dark square with simplified geometric candle cones instead of the tall photographic candle image shown in the source
Inset bottleneck block is small and its chip labels (BN/ReLU/Conv) are tiny and cramped compared to the large, legible inset in the source
Slab stacks appear front-on with little visible depth in the default view, whereas the source slabs clearly show their top/side faces via oblique projection
The two '1000' classifier labels sit very close together and nearly merge, unlike the clearly separated twin bars in the source
Source shows dashed arrow leaders connecting block totals between stages; only generic dashed dimension leaders are present
evaluation.notes: A faithful, recognizable ResNet-50-style architecture figure with all major elements (input, conv/maxpool slab, four ResBlock stages, subsample arrows, dimension callouts, bottleneck inset with skip connection, 1000-class output) and rich, functional interactions; weaknesses are the cramped inset, simplified input image, and nearly overlapping '1000' labels.
action_items: Enlarge the inset panel and its chip labels so the BN/ReLU/Conv sequence is comfortably readable like the source
Separate the two '1000' classifier labels/bars so they are clearly distinct
Make the input image plate taller and more photo-like (or reduce the candle abstraction) to better match the source's portrait image
Tilt the default view slightly more obliquely so slab top/side faces are visible without dragging

feedback.rationale: Concept accuracy is 5/5, interactivity is 5/5, overall average is 4.4 with no failure modes — remaining action items are minor visual polish (inset size, label spacing, camera tilt) that don't warrant another iteration.
